You said: sappho 31sappho 31
Sappho 31 is a famous ancient Greek lyric poem describing the intense physical and emotional symptoms of falling in love and jealousy. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHrOzAVsl5VO3fQ7hFhAnv9J88B0JZWpB-bNVitiEyjZoH7qk5UUO0SBdFhfUf7LHAvtUG3R8a9v_dViYsY5rIqOg0FqFKJzAsjpLE9lbISS6zJVBML8tPTcihvcCW4), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVjh5jkPpNhLwLuUZgLz11Had4rJQ-l4-Mw4EWbVKqiZSqC7ZHfnG76OULH7iBrO16FYV9jxfZd9i5B29t3TsG8-ouzYcbWQDiyR57DjN07z0JPwySLCjFGL8WCP2s6AOguQ)]
Overview of the Poem

* Author: [Sappho](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHrOzAVsl5VO3fQ7hFhAnv9J88B0JZWpB-bNVitiEyjZoH7qk5UUO0SBdFhfUf7LHAvtUG3R8a9v_dViYsY5rIqOg0FqFKJzAsjpLE9lbISS6zJVBML8tPTcihvcCW4) of Lesbos, written in the Archaic period around the 6th century BCE.
* Alternative Names: Known as phainetai moi ("It seems to me") or the Ode to Anactoria.
* Preservation: Survives mostly intact because a later ancient critic quoted it in the treatise [On the Sublime](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVjh5jkPpNhLwLuUZgLz11Had4rJQ-l4-Mw4EWbVKqiZSqC7ZHfnG76OULH7iBrO16FYV9jxfZd9i5B29t3TsG8-ouzYcbWQDiyR57DjN07z0JPwySLCjFGL8WCP2s6AOguQ). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAVsL1spfayNDX-DHyFVpOix6c_yDpR8YeP1yVuPJPK9bngu8Iip-m6bsZ9H0JhqQlNNpNqqn05-bBdDsqaF4Pc89P7nyj73wbpJp9hgBekQVEetu1k4gd4ytZjhCHSVQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEB6zswFUGxWgVPolPEXDryR761QROegu4ZSKZ9m2uGnOBBi4ifoROs-IXZU6GmUkzyZ7OB_gJyo49HDkFpgzQNtASmNgOO77Vm9OiCtevRzx48Uvhs95pXV67SleDlExAmP5f3quFwXyM2xO85VoZgGjtdt2yKDZ4nT4fIAl_DSKcb7XYrhmmgDqkQrdNVxfc), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHrOzAVsl5VO3fQ7hFhAnv9J88B0JZWpB-bNVitiEyjZoH7qk5UUO0SBdFhfUf7LHAvtUG3R8a9v_dViYsY5rIqOg0FqFKJzAsjpLE9lbISS6zJVBML8tPTcihvcCW4), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVjh5jkPpNhLwLuUZgLz11Had4rJQ-l4-Mw4EWbVKqiZSqC7ZHfnG76OULH7iBrO16FYV9jxfZd9i5B29t3TsG8-ouzYcbWQDiyR57DjN07z0JPwySLCjFGL8WCP2s6AOguQ)]

What the Poem Describes

* The Scene: The speaker watches a man sitting close to a beloved woman, listening to her talk and laugh. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEB6zswFYu2PlRSZlkpwEjmf4_DotfaCkWoFTT9x_uwQcsk1Y8hmUNrNykmAkjKJsjd9oWgZgxaYtZzmX_jUr9MMSNBACMZESesOonGHNFIQvYsMIJrbBTCJOT5M2vkwQdrr2-vmd1FckQ7BJQ2MTe9R2dAVKvqoHfYC5VUcpsyLDtZ-eX3xW98YV5kNC7IHyFJlsVJlP6xc6f5wpQANe7eGZpY4lc), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEB6zswFUGxWgVPolPEXDryR761QROegu4ZSKZ9m2uGnOBBi4ifoROs-IXZU6GmUkzyZ7OB_gJyo49HDkFpgzQNtASmNgOO77Vm9OiCtevRzx48Uvhs95pXV67SleDlExAmP5f3quFwXyM2xO85VoZgGjtdt2yKDZ4nT4fIAl_DSKcb7XYrhmmgDqkQrdNVxfc)]
* The Reaction: The speaker feels overwhelmed by a mix of jealousy, desire, and physical shock. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESvwEB6zswFVWoGOU6IjtYlRvq_MkTQutXXK18dsGP2G-SPy0CC2ZtRCGfTkH-ZczpeFDtdbyRCzYxALBf5hF8de12B-kmeOOUFIiTtSi4kxV3v5me3MkOwnmLSaKGwsosB5RjjH5-SKIkcYSAvuo5uEkiAG_bcl3eBas6EyQsPZxk1aJUMgh4jki7aUFwE-0bPinnfkhCyg-cL8Vb4BYaNh7aQI6VWYCDWyZxPrTp2GPN2UIF45M4TyHRdpIjq_BUnA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVjh5jkPpNhLwLuUZgLz11Had4rJQ-l4-Mw4EWbVKqiZSqC7ZHfnG76OULH7iBrO16FYV9jxfZd9i5B29t3TsG8-ouzYcbWQDiyR57DjN07z0JPwySLCjFGL8WCP2s6AOguQ)]
* The Symptoms: The poem famously lists bodily reactions like a racing heart, a silent tongue, ringing ears, cold sweat, and feeling close to death. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVjh5jkPpNhLwLuUZgLz11Had4rJQ-l4-Mw4EWbVKqiZSqC7ZHfnG76OULH7iBrO16FYV9jxfZd9i5B29t3TsG8-ouzYcbWQDiyR57DjN07z0JPwySLCjFGL8WCP2s6AOguQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEB6zswFYu2PlRSZlkpwEjmf4_DotfaCkWoFTT9x_uwQcsk1Y8hmUNrNykmAkjKJsjd9oWgZgxaYtZzmX_jUr9MMSNBACMZESesOonGHNFIQvYsMIJrbBTCJOT5M2vkwQdrr2-vmd1FckQ7BJQ2MTe9R2dAVKvqoHfYC5VUcpsyLDtZ-eX3xW98YV5kNC7IHyFJlsVJlP6xc6f5wpQANe7eGZpY4lc)]
